title: Rapidus Partners with 17 Design Firms to Secure 2Nm Chip Buyers
key_facts: Rapidus has partnered with 17 design firms, including Synopsys and Infosys, to secure buyers for its planned two-nanometre foundry.
The venture holds $15 billion in government funding.
Commercial fabrication is planned for the second half of the next fiscal year in Chitose, Hokkaido; a pilot line is already operating.
Rapidus is developing its 2nm process with IBM.
Landing customer commitments is the main hurdle against TSMC, Samsung (2nm chips since last year) and Intel.
Pilot yields will face customer evaluation through 2027 before volume tools are installed.
An initial public offering is targeted around the fiscal year ending March 2032.
quote_evidence: Japan's state-backed chipmaker Rapidus has partnered with 17 design firms to secure buyers for its planned two-nanometre foundry.
Landing customer commitments remains the primary operational hurdle.
Rapidus management has set an initial public offering target for around the fiscal year ending March 2032 to open private equity participation and reduce reliance on state funding.
why_it_matters_hint: Rapidus needs customers before its 2nm factory starts, and now has 17 design partners.
